question: Mahendravarman I who wrote Mattavilasa-prahasana is related to which of the following ruling dynasties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pallava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahendravarman I was a ruler of the **Pallava dynasty** who ruled over the southern part of India during the early 7th century.
 
• He is known for his patronage of arts and architecture, particularly for initiating the rock-cut architecture in Mahabalipuram.
 
• Mahendravarman I was a versatile scholar and a playwright, and he composed the famous Sanskrit play **Mattavilasa-prahasana** (The Delight of the Drunkards).
 
• The Pallavas were instrumental in the promotion of Tamil literature and culture, and they contributed significantly to the growth of Dravidian architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maitraka Dynasty**

 
 
• The Maitrakas ruled parts of present-day Gujarat from the late 5th century to the 8th century.
 
• They were known for their patronage of learning and religion, particularly Buddhism and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Pushyabhuti Dynasty**
 
 
• The Pushyabhuti dynasty, also known as the Vardhana dynasty, ruled parts of northern India in the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• The most notable ruler of this dynasty was Harsha Vardhana, who extended his empire across much of North India.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• The Chalukyas were a major dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and the 12th centuries.
 
• They are known for their contributions to art, architecture, and literature, particularly in the Deccan region.
